Oct 24 : Burnley have parted ways with head coach Nicky Hayen after just 14 matches, the Championship club said on Saturday, following a poor start to the season. The 46-year-old Belgian's final game in charge was Saturday's 4-1 defeat at Lincoln City, a result that extended Burnley's struggles and left them 22nd in the table. Burnley have won only once in their last 12 league matches. "Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect. The Board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season," the club said in a statement. Hayen was appointed on a three-year deal in the summer, replacing Scott Parker, who left by mutual consent in April after Burnley's relegation from the Premier League was confirmed, with the club dropping into the Championship for the third time in five seasons

After being appointed on a permanent basis in June 2024, he also won the Belgian Cup and Belgian Super Cup and was named Belgium's Coach of the Year in 2024.

NAPLES, Italy, Oct 24 : Napoli midfielder Frank Anguissa scored with a superb overhead kick but AS Roma twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw in a pulsating Serie A clash in Naples, while Como kept up their good form with a 2-0 home win against Sassuolo. Roma could have gone top of the table with victory but, having trailed 2-0 and then 3-2 late on, will be pleased with a point as they also preserved their 15-game unbeaten run in Serie A that dates back to April. They are in third place with 18 points from eight games, one point behind leaders Inter Milan and Lazio, who have each played a game fewer. Napoli will be disappointed not to have managed the game better as Anguissa’s spectacular overhead kick gave them the lead and Scott McTominay doubled the advantage.

At that stage they were cruising, but two goals in four minutes from Matias Soule and Leonardo Balerdi drew Roma level. When McTominay added his second in the closing stages the momentum swung back in Napoli’s favour, but Balerdi headed an equaliser for Roma with a minute remaining. Two second-half goals from Anastasios Douvikas took Como to victory against Sassuolo as the Greek striker continued his red-hot form. He has scored five goals in his last four games in all competitions and provided two clinical finishes in the box as Como climbed to fourth place with 17 points from their eight games. Sassuolo are in 14th. "He (Douvikas) is growing in a way that could make him a very, very important centre-forward," Como coach Cesc Fabregas said. "In the last three years he has been one of those signings that has given a lot of satisfaction." Bologna were 2-0 winners at Cagliari as they claimed their second victory of the season. Defender Nicolo Casale scored his first goal in almost four years to give Bologna the lead before Federico Bernardeschi doubled the advantage for the visitors. "It was a very difficult game on a tough pitch," Bernardeschi said. "These games are won with character. Cagliari made us suffer, but in the second half we reacted well."

Source: Reuters

LONDON, Oct 24 : Gabriel Magalhaes proved Arsenal's hero at both ends of the pitch on Saturday as the reigning champions beat Everton 2-0 to draw level with Manchester City at the Premier League summit. Making his 200th Premier League appearance, the centre back was instrumental in a victory that put Arsenal level on 21 points with City, the Brazilian combining defensive authority at the back with a decisive goal that put the result beyond doubt. "He's one of the best centre backs in the world, no question, with the impact he has in both boxes," Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said. "His leadership, his presence, what he offers to the rest of the boys is unique and we're very happy to have him."

With his regular partner William Saliba still absent through injury, Gabriel's importance to Arsenal was underlined when Everton struggled to establish a foothold in the pouring rain at Emirates Stadium. Gabriel consistently got the better of Everton striker Thierno Barry, who had a frustrating afternoon repeatedly ending up on the slick turf and pounding the ground in frustration after losing several duels with the defender. Gabriel also came to Arsenal's rescue when goalkeeper David Raya failed to deal convincingly with an Everton corner in the first half, clearing the danger off the line to preserve the north London side's advantage. There was a brief injury scare after an awkward landing when Gabriel jarred his knee on the turf, but he quickly returned to score the decisive second goal in the 68th minute. After his centre back partner Ezri Konsa had opened the scoring from a corner in the seventh minute - Arsenal's first set-piece goal since May - Gabriel rose at the back post to meet Ben White's floated cross to head home their second. "Gabi was unbelievable, the action that leads to the possible injury and then the way he overcomes that situation with his willingness to go again and to score that goal," Arteta added. "It's a great description of what he is as a player and as a leader in this club." It was Gabriel's 21st Premier League goal for Arsenal - more than any other defender since he made his debut in the competition six years ago. "Very pleased for him. He's a top, top player. Top human being. Very happy for him," Konsa said. "He's made my life easy since I've joined the club and it's been a pleasure playing alongside him."

Source: Reuters

DORTMUND, Germany, Oct 24 : Maximilian Beier scored a superb winner as Borussia Dortmund went top of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 home victory over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday, while RB Leipzig swept aside promoted Elversberg 4-0 after a rampant second-half display. Dortmund have 17 points from their seven matches, three points ahead of second-placed Bayern Munich, who have a game in hand and play on Sunday at Freiburg. The home side had been frustrated until Beier picked up the ball on the edge of the box, made space for the shot and curled his effort into the far corner of the net. The result ends a run of consecutive draws for Dortmund and is another clean sheet for a side who have conceded only four goals this season.

CARDOSO DOUBLE Romulo Cardoso scored twice for RB Leipzig in their thumping win, while Tidiam Gomis and Christoph Baumgartner, in his first Bundesliga game of the season after injury, were also on target. Elversberg have acquitted themselves well in their maiden top-flight season but were well beaten. Werder Bremen climbed to sixth with a 3-2 victory at Mainz as a pair of Niclas Fuellkrug penalties inside the opening 25 minutes gave them the perfect start. Mainz pulled back a goal but Ludovit Reis made it 3-1 and despite the hosts netting again, Bremen were able to hold on for the win. Fuellkrug took his tally of goals this season to eight and leads the scorers' charts in the Bundesliga having scored in his last six league matches. Rayan Philippe netted a winning goal two minutes from the end as Paderborn moved out of the bottom three with a 1-0 win at home to Hamburg.  Philippe joined Paderborn on loan from Hamburg this season and came off the bench against his parent club, choosing not to celebrate despite the enormity of the goal for his side. There was a goal and a red card each for Augsburg and Union Berlin as they drew 1-1. Both teams were down to 10 men before the first goal was scored as Felix Uduokhai got his marching orders for Union and Juma Bah was sent off for the home side. Han-Noah Massengo put the hosts ahead in the 71st minute but they had to settle for a point when Janik Haberer equalised for the visitors three minutes later. Cologne and Schalke played out a 0-0 draw, a result that left Schalke in the bottom three.

Source: Reuters

BIRMINGHAM, England, Oct 24 : Manchester City's perfect start to the Premier League season came to an abrupt end at Villa Park on Saturday when two costly mistakes condemned Enzo Maresca's side to a 2-1 defeat despite them dominating large stretches of the contest. City arrived in Birmingham having won all seven of their league matches but a pair of defensive blunders gave Aston Villa their chances and they took both.  Marc Guehi's early miscontrol allowed John McGinn to set up Nicolas Jackson for the opening goal, while goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma allowed Jackson's low shot to squirm underneath him after the hour mark. The result was particularly frustrating for City given the balance of play. They registered seven shots on target to Villa's two and repeatedly forced Zion Suzuki into action, but the Japan goalkeeper produced a string of excellent saves to preserve the hosts' lead.

There was at least one positive for City with Erling Haaland scoring on his return from a foot injury. The Norwegian had sat out Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League rout of AEK Athens but headed home from Iliman Ndiaye's cross for City's lone goal. The afternoon belonged instead to Suzuki, who continued to justify Villa's faith since they signed him in August to replace the departed Emi Martinez. Time and again he denied City, frustrating Haaland and company as Villa claimed their fourth successive home league victory over the Blues.  Maresca was left to lament his side's wastefulness and the two avoidable goals that ultimately decided the match. "Performance overall was good, amount of chances we created. "Absolutely, both (goals were avoidable). Sometimes you have to be a bit more lucky because we only conceded those two chances. But we created a lot of chances. "We played most of the game in their box but you have to be clinical and avoid mistakes like the two goals we conceded." For Villa, after a turbulent summer of arrivals and departures - including Martinez who went to Chelsea - there were finally signs that Unai Emery's rebuilt side are beginning to settle after a poor league start of three losses from their first four games. "Today was a really good test, I was so excited for this test," Emery said. "Today is one step forward." City have little time to dwell on the defeat, with back-to-back meetings against high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion next on the agenda, first in the League Cup fourth round on Wednesday and then in the Premier League next Saturday. "A top team, another one," City defender Ruben Dias said. "A different way to play so we'll make the adaptation then focus on ourselves that's the main thing - our spirit, our will to win."

Source: Reuters

Oct 24 : Former Pakistan Twenty20 captain Salman Ali Agha, who was among seven players released mid-series after the side lost two tests to England in August, has returned to the test squad for next month's two-match series with Sri Lanka at home, the Pakistan Cricket Board said on Saturday. Agha was removed as Pakistan's T20 captain and left out of this month's T20 series against Sri Lanka but the 32-year-old impressed in the One-Day Internationals, scoring a century against Sri Lanka last Sunday.  Left-arm spinner Ali Usman, who was also among the players released during the England tour, has been named in the 14-man squad as well, with the first test set to begin on November 9 at Rawalpindi. Babar Azam will continue to lead Pakistan as they look to bounce back from a 3-0 series loss in England.

SOELDEN, Austria, Oct 24 : Paula Moltzan started the World Cup Alpine ski season with a first career victory at the age of 32 on Saturday after US teammate Mikaela Shiffrin blew a giant slalom first-leg lead and finished seventh in the Austrian resort of Soelden. The 2026 Olympic team combined bronze medallist beat Italian-born Lara Colturi, who skis for Albania, by the slimmest of margins - 0.01 of a second after two runs down the Rettenbach glacier slope - with Germany's Emma Aicher third. The victory from fifth after the first run also made Moltzan the first woman to win with Van Deer skis, the brand founded by Austria's retired eight-times overall World Cup winner Marcel Hirscher. "It feels like a fairytale right now," said the Minnesota-born skier.

"It doesn't really feel real but we've put in a lot of hard work this summer developing the ski and it feels like this is kind of a pinnacle, that it's paying off and we did all the right things. I can't imagine a better start." The podium was the 11th of Moltzan's career, six of them second places including one in Soelden a year ago when Austrian Julia Scheib was a first-time winner. Scheib did not finish the first run this time. World Cup overall champion Shiffrin led by 0.14 seconds after the first run, with Sweden's Sara Hector second and Switzerland's Camille Rast third, but conditions changed for the later starters in the second leg with falling snow, flat light and grey skies. The 31-year-old US great, chasing a record-extending 111th World Cup win, has not won a giant slalom since December 2023 but has shifted her focus this season towards that discipline and super-G, and will race fewer slaloms. Saturday's race also marked the World Cup return of Slovakian Petra Vlhova, who had been out injured since January 2024. The 2022 Olympic slalom champion and 2021 overall World Cup winner finished 23rd.     Italian Federica Brignone, the Olympic champion in giant slalom and super-G on home snow in Cortina in February, was absent as she continues her recovery from surgery in August.

(Writing by Alan Baldwin, editing by Ken Ferris)

Oct 24 : Arsenal joined Manchester City at the top of the Premier League table after a 2-0 victory over Everton in torrential rain at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, capitalising on City's first defeat of the season earlier in the day. City had left the door open when they fell to a 2-1 loss at Aston Villa, where Nicolas Jackson struck twice to end the visitors' perfect start to the league campaign. Tottenham Hotspur stunned fourth-placed Chelsea 2-0 in only their second league victory at Stamford Bridge in 36 years, while Fulham beat Coventry City 1-0 for their second league victory of the season. With the leaders beaten in Birmingham, Arsenal seized their chance to erase the three-point gap as goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel secured a comfortable win over Everton in soaking north London conditions.

The result moved Mikel Arteta's side level on 21 points with City in what is already shaping up to be a closely fought title race after eight games, but one played under a cloud amid City's off-field financial case. STRONG START Arsenal made their strong start count when Martin Odegaard's corner caused chaos in the Everton box. England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford kept out the initial danger after the ball was flicked on at the near post but, with Everton unable to clear, Konsa bundled home his first goal for the club from a yard out in the seventh minute. The set-piece goal was Arsenal's first since May, ending a run of 13 games across all competitions without one. "I've come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us," Konsa said. "It's not surprising to me. "We are champions and to be champions you've got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible." Arsenal's two milestone men combined to give the Gunners a two-goal cushion in the 68th minute, with Ben White marking his 200th appearance for the club by clipping a cross to the far post, where Gabriel headed home on his 200th Premier League appearance. Everton are ninth in the table.    JACKSON DOUBLE At Villa Park, Unai Emery's team climbed to sixth on 11 points with their first home league victory this season and third successive league win over City, who are playing under the shadow of an independent commission's findings that they committed 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules. City have always denied any wrongdoing, and have appealed. Jackson took advantage of two City blunders, opening the scoring in the sixth minute when defender Marc Guehi's heavy touch allowed Villa captain John McGinn to pounce and feed the striker, who slotted the ball into the bottom corner. Erling Haaland equalised soon after the break when he headed home Iliman Ndiaye's clipped cross from a free kick. But Jackson struck the winner on the hour when Ibrahim Mbaye surged down the right before cutting the ball back for his Senegal international teammate, whose shot sneaked under the diving body of keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. "It was incredible, we got the win which is the most important thing. Man City are a strong team, the league leaders," Jackson told TNT Sports. "It's just the beginning, we're trying to work game by game." At Stamford Bridge, Spurs got on the scoresheet in the 77th minute when Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders punched a corner into his own net in his first league start. Chelsea were reduced to 10 men when Cole Palmer was shown a second yellow card in the 80th minute for a late challenge on Conor Gallagher. Mathys Tel sealed the victory for Spurs in the 87th when he gained possession inside his own half before embarking on a surging run down the left, gliding past two defenders and firing a low shot from outside the box into the bottom corner. "It's very special, because we came here a lot of times and didn't get a win," said Tel. "And today, we made it together, all together, we showed great mentality, and I'm very happy about it." Spurs climbed to 12th with the win. At Coventry, Fulham appeared ready to substitute Oscar Bobb before the winger produced a moment of quality in the 80th minute, driving into the box and curling a superb finish into the far corner. Fulham are 13th in the table, while Coventry are 19th.

Source: Reuters

Oct 24 : Defending Ningbo Open champion Elena Rybakina overcame Russian sixth seed Diana Shnaider 6-3 7-5 in the semi-final on Saturday to reach another title clash and remind rivals of her threat ahead of next month's WTA Finals. The world number one will face Leylah Fernandez in the final on Sunday after the unseeded Canadian beat Czech Marie Bouzkova by the same 6-3 7-5 scoreline in the earlier semi at the Yinzhou International Tennis Centre in the eastern Chinese city. Australian and US Open champion Rybakina, who arrived for her title defence after a bruising defeat in Beijing and a foot injury that forced her out of Wuhan, showed flashes of her best form despite a few wobbles against the 13th-ranked Shnaider. "She (Shnaider) played really well and it's always difficult to play against left-handers. We don't have so many on the tour," said Rybakina, who faces a similar test against Fernandez.

"I needed some time. The returns were not as bad but during the rallies to switch the pattern was a little bit of an issue for me, but I'm happy I managed to win in two sets." An aggressive start with powerful winners from deep helped three-times Grand Slam winner Rybakina take full control of the opening frame, which she sealed on her 11th set point after a sudden dip in form. 'SO MANY OPPORTUNITIES' "It was an important game and it was a long one," added the top-seeded Rybakina. "It was on my serve and it was a struggle ... I was playing the first balls really well but I couldn't close the game ... so many opportunities, but I'm glad it went my way. She played some great shots and great rallies." The 27-year-old continued to struggle with the accuracy of her first serve in the next set, but won the crucial points and carved out a 4-3 advantage with a break, only to be broken to love in the 10th game. Rybakina responded strongly to get her nose in front again in the next game with some big hitting, before closing out the victory with a much more assured display on serve to take her place in the final. She will aim to further sharpen her game in Sunday's final before turning her attention to the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo next week and then launching her WTA Finals title defence at Indian Wells from November 8. "It's never easy," Rybakina said about winning back-to-back trophies at the Ningbo Open. "Of course I'll try to do my best. I'm going to fight and give my all tomorrow."

Source: Reuters

Oct 24 : India's middle-order batter Tilak Varma hammered a half-century off 25 balls as India chased down a target of 181 with a ball to spare, taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match Twenty20 series with New Zealand on Saturday. New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner's destructive spell (4-21) had left India shaken, with 68 runs needed from the last five overs. But Varma (51) and Nitish Kumar Reddy (26) targeted the pacers in the final three overs to secure a four-wicket win. "The Hyderabadi boys were in play today ... what everyone believed, I have done it, so I'm really proud of myself," said player-of-the-match Varma, who partnered with Reddy to add 69 runs off 30 balls for the seventh wicket. The Christchurch pitch looked slower than in Thursday's high-scoring contest as India's pacers restricted New Zealand to 43-3 during the powerplay, but Glenn Phillips (70) and Bevon Jacobs (58) turned the innings around, adding 116 for the fourth wicket.

Phillips scored his second straight fifty as he hit four boundaries and four sixes before Arshdeep Singh (2-33) got him caught near the fence. Michael Bracewell then scored 10 off two balls to help the hosts reach 180-5. INDIA OVERCOME SHAKY START India's reply got off to a shaky start with Sanju Samson (14) playing out a maiden in the first over before edging Jacob Duffy's slower ball to point. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who replaced the injured Ishan Kishan, scored four before falling to Nathan Smith. Santner's left-arm spin added to the damage, sending back opener Abhishek Sharma (27) before bowling India captain Shreyas Iyer (7) with a flighted ball. Two balls later, Axar Patel nearly cleared the long on boundary but Finn Allen jumped to catch it over his shoulder, tossing it to Daryl Mitchell before he landed over the rope. Naman Dhir, who had helped close out India's chase on Thursday, fought back with a quick 31 off 17 balls, but he too fell to Santner, caught at extra cover to leave India reeling at 112-6 in the 15th over. But Varma, in at number six, hit Duffy for two boundaries before punishing Smith with three fours and a six, getting India within 11 runs of victory with one over left. Varma hit Duffy for four off the second ball of the final over to ease the pressure, before Reddy brought up the winning runs with a shot down mid on. "I feel every individual in our team is a match-winner ... we thought the game was going away from us, but Tilak and Nitish showed immense character," said Iyer. India can seal the series with a win at Wellington on Tuesday.

Source: Reuters

Oct 24 : FIFA president Gianni Infantino laughed off questions about whether he had considered resigning in the wake of the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, pointing to overwhelming support from member associations around the globe. Three months after facing calls to resign after he abandoned the proposal that sought private investment in a new entity controlling commercial rights linked to major FIFA competitions, Infantino now finds himself in a position of strength. His prospects for reelection strengthened on Friday after the head of Asian football endorsed him for a fourth term, with Asian Football confederation (AFC) President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa saying Asia was united behind Infantino. "I was elected by 211 member associations from all over the world. I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view," Infantino told the BBC as he laughed off a question about whether he had considered stepping down.

"But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone ... then we need to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority. "I'm just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all African countries have endorsed me. I'm speaking to all associations everywhere in the world." The AFC had previously joined European body UEFA and CONCACAF, which represents North and Central America and the Caribbean, in criticising the FFE proposal. But a divided CONCACAF and the AFC's U-turn have left Europe increasingly isolated while exposing the lack of a viable alternative candidate for the FIFA presidency. Infantino is seeking a fourth term until 2031 and potential candidates must submit their nominations by November 18. He apologised at a FIFA Council meeting in Zurich last week over the way the FFE proposal was handled but that did not sway European football associations such as Germany and England. However, the 56-year-old Swiss-Italian administrator added: "It's OK to disagree ... but then we need to be able to move on. "There are different points of view. It's not always easy to bring them all under one roof, but we need to respect and I do respect all opinions all views," Infantino added. "Then it will be up to the FIFA member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want FIFA to be run."

Source: Reuters
